overviewHtml:
This graded quiz assesses your understanding of how to work with AI on real tasks. You'll be asked about writing prompts and supplying context and examples, diagnosing a poor output, what studies of professionals found, roles for AI in writing and analysis, and permissions, prompt injection, and checkpoints for AI agents.

Note: Aim for a score of 80 percent or higher. If you score lower, use the feedback to review the topics you missed, then retake the quiz.

forms.stemHtml: Which of these should a prompt state so that a model can do a task well? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: What the result is for
options.text: What the result is for
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The goal tells the model what purpose the result has to serve.

options.html: Who will read the result
options.text: Who will read the result
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The audience, and what they already know, shapes what the result should say.

options.html: What limits the result must stay within
options.text: What limits the result must stay within
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Constraints such as length, tone, and what to leave out are things the model can't guess.

options.html: How hard the model should try
options.text: How hard the model should try
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on what a model needs to be told.

forms.stemHtml: An AI assistant is asked what a company's refund policy says, and it isn't given the policy. What will its answer be based on?

options.html: General patterns of what refund policies usually say
options.text: General patterns of what refund policies usually say
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Without your material, a model draws on the typical case from its training, so the answer is generic.

options.html: The company's own policy, recalled from its training data
options.text: The company's own policy, recalled from its training data
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on supplying context.

options.html: The refund policy of the company that built the assistant
options.text: The refund policy of the company that built the assistant
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on supplying context.

options.html: Nothing, since it can't answer without the policy text
options.text: Nothing, since it can't answer without the policy text
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on supplying context.

forms.stemHtml: A prompt includes one sample email. The output repeats the sample's greeting and its deadline, though neither fits the new message. What is this called?

options.html: Grounding in the source material
options.text: Grounding in the source material
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on examples in a prompt.

options.html: Over-copying of the example
options.text: Over-copying of the example
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The model reused the example's particular details where only its general pattern was wanted.

options.html: A missing output format
options.text: A missing output format
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on examples in a prompt.

options.html: A compounding error across steps
options.text: A compounding error across steps
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on examples in a prompt.

forms.stemHtml: An output is generic and states two facts about your project wrongly. Which gap in the prompt does this most likely point to?

options.html: A missing example of the style you wanted
options.text: A missing example of the style you wanted
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on iteration.

options.html: A missing constraint on the output's length
options.text: A missing constraint on the output's length
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on iteration.

options.html: Missing context about the project
options.text: Missing context about the project
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Generic output with wrong facts means the model lacked the documents, facts, or background.

options.html: A missing statement of the tone you wanted
options.text: A missing statement of the tone you wanted
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on iteration.

forms.stemHtml: What does "skill leveling" refer to in studies of AI at work?

options.html: Experts gaining more from AI tools than beginners do
options.text: Experts gaining more from AI tools than beginners do
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on controlled studies of AI at work.

options.html: Workers losing their own skills after long use of AI tools
options.text: Workers losing their own skills after long use of AI tools
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on controlled studies of AI at work.

options.html: AI tools reaching the skill of the best human workers
options.text: AI tools reaching the skill of the best human workers
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on controlled studies of AI at work.

options.html: A narrower gap between weaker and stronger workers
options.text: A narrower gap between weaker and stronger workers
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Skill leveling is a narrowing of the gap between weaker and stronger performers when both use the same tool.

forms.stemHtml: What is the main risk of having AI write the first draft of a document?

options.html: It sets the frame before you've thought
options.text: It sets the frame before you've thought
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A draft arrives with a structure, an emphasis, and a conclusion already chosen, and you end up reacting to them.

options.html: It takes longer than writing it yourself
options.text: It takes longer than writing it yourself
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the four roles for AI in writing.

options.html: It can't produce text in a formal tone
options.text: It can't produce text in a formal tone
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the four roles for AI in writing.

options.html: It leaves out every fact you supplied
options.text: It leaves out every fact you supplied
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the four roles for AI in writing.

forms.stemHtml: An AI assistant extracts ten findings from a report you supplied. What makes the findings quickest to check?

options.html: A confidence score beside each finding
options.text: A confidence score beside each finding
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on analysis from your own sources.

options.html: A second list of findings from the same model
options.text: A second list of findings from the same model
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on analysis from your own sources.

options.html: A shorter list with only the top five findings
options.text: A shorter list with only the top five findings
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on analysis from your own sources.

options.html: The passage that supports each finding
options.text: The passage that supports each finding
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! With the supporting passage, you can find it in the report and see whether it says what the model claims.

forms.stemHtml: What does least privilege mean when you grant access to an AI agent?

options.html: Granting full access once the agent has proved reliable
options.text: Granting full access once the agent has proved reliable
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on permissions and excessive agency.

options.html: Granting only the access the task needs
options.text: Granting only the access the task needs
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Least privilege is the practice of granting only the access a task needs and nothing more.

options.html: Granting access only to tools from one developer
options.text: Granting access only to tools from one developer
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on permissions and excessive agency.

options.html: Granting access only during your working hours
options.text: Granting access only during your working hours
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on permissions and excessive agency.

forms.stemHtml: Which abilities, when combined in one AI agent, make up the lethal trifecta? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Access to private data
options.text: Access to private data
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Private data is what an attacker would be after.

options.html: Exposure to untrusted content
options.text: Exposure to untrusted content
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Content written by someone else is how a hidden instruction reaches the agent.

options.html: Use of more than one AI model
options.text: Use of more than one AI model
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on prompt injection and the lethal trifecta.

options.html: A way to communicate externally
options.text: A way to communicate externally
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! An outside channel is how private data would be carried away.

forms.stemHtml: Before which of these actions does an approval step matter most? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Sending a message to a client
options.text: Sending a message to a client
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A sent message reaches someone else and can't be called back.

options.html: Deleting a folder of files
options.text: Deleting a folder of files
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A deletion can destroy something that can't be recovered.

options.html: Saving a draft for you to review
options.text: Saving a draft for you to review
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on checkpoints and reversibility.

options.html: Making a payment
options.text: Making a payment
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A payment is costly or impossible to undo.

forms.stemHtml: A prompt reads, "Write a notice about the parking changes." Which additions would give the model information it lacks? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: "The notice should get staff to move their cars by Friday."
options.text: "The notice should get staff to move their cars by Friday."
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This states the goal: what the notice is for.

options.html: "Make it a truly excellent and impressive notice."
options.text: "Make it a truly excellent and impressive notice."
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on what a model needs to be told.

options.html: "The readers are staff who haven't heard about the changes."
options.text: "The readers are staff who haven't heard about the changes."
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This states the audience and what they already know.

options.html: "Keep it under 100 words, and don't name the contractor."
options.text: "Keep it under 100 words, and don't name the contractor."
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This states constraints: a length and something to leave out.

forms.stemHtml: What does "grounding" mean when you work with an AI model?

options.html: Limiting the model to short and factual answers
options.text: Limiting the model to short and factual answers
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on supplying context.

options.html: Asking the model to rate its own confidence
options.text: Asking the model to rate its own confidence
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on supplying context.

options.html: Having it work from material that you supply
options.text: Having it work from material that you supply
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Grounding means the model works from your material instead of from the general patterns of its training.

options.html: Training the model again on your own documents
options.text: Training the model again on your own documents
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on supplying context.

forms.stemHtml: Which step best reduces the chance that a model copies the incidental details of an example?

options.html: Making the single example much longer
options.text: Making the single example much longer
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on examples in a prompt.

options.html: Placing the example ahead of the instruction
options.text: Placing the example ahead of the instruction
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on examples in a prompt.

options.html: Removing the instruction and keeping the example
options.text: Removing the instruction and keeping the example
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on examples in a prompt.

options.html: Using varied examples that share the pattern
options.text: Using varied examples that share the pattern
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! When examples differ in their details and share what matters, the shared features stand out as the pattern.

forms.stemHtml: An output has the right content, but its layout and tone aren't what you wanted. Which gap in the prompt does this most likely point to?

options.html: A missing example of the output
options.text: A missing example of the output
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! When the content is right and the style or shape is off, a sample of what you want is the usual fix.

options.html: Missing facts about the situation
options.text: Missing facts about the situation
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on iteration.

options.html: A missing statement of the purpose
options.text: A missing statement of the purpose
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on iteration.

options.html: Missing source documents to draw on
options.text: Missing source documents to draw on
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on iteration.

forms.stemHtml: A study followed 5,172 customer support agents whose company introduced an AI tool. Which group improved the most?

options.html: The most experienced and highest-skilled agents
options.text: The most experienced and highest-skilled agents
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on controlled studies of AI at work.

options.html: Less experienced and lower-skilled agents
options.text: Less experienced and lower-skilled agents
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Newer and lower-skilled agents improved in both speed and quality, while the most experienced saw small quality declines.

options.html: Agents who chose to ignore the tool's suggestions
options.text: Agents who chose to ignore the tool's suggestions
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on controlled studies of AI at work.

options.html: Agents who handled the fewest customer chats
options.text: Agents who handled the fewest customer chats
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on controlled studies of AI at work.

forms.stemHtml: A manager has an AI assistant draft a proposal and spends an hour adjusting the wording. In the meeting, she can't explain why the proposal recommends what it does. What happened?

options.html: The assistant summarized her notes and dropped a point
options.text: The assistant summarized her notes and dropped a point
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the four roles for AI in writing.

options.html: The assistant edited her text and flattened her voice
options.text: The assistant edited her text and flattened her voice
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the four roles for AI in writing.

options.html: The draft chose the reasoning before she did
options.text: The draft chose the reasoning before she did
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! With AI as drafter, the structure and conclusion were set before she had thought, and she edited within them.

options.html: The assistant gave objections that turned out wrong
options.text: The assistant gave objections that turned out wrong
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the four roles for AI in writing.

forms.stemHtml: An assistant gives you a finding along with a quoted passage from your document. What should you do before relying on the finding?

options.html: Find the passage in the original document
options.text: Find the passage in the original document
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A model can produce a quotation that isn't in the document, so the passage has to be found in the original.

options.html: Ask the assistant whether the quotation is exact
options.text: Ask the assistant whether the quotation is exact
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on analysis from your own sources.

options.html: Accept it, since a quotation was provided
options.text: Accept it, since a quotation was provided
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on analysis from your own sources.

options.html: Ask for the same finding in different words
options.text: Ask for the same finding in different words
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on analysis from your own sources.

forms.stemHtml: An agent's only job is to tell you each morning which meetings you have that day. Which grant fits least privilege?

options.html: Read and write access to your calendar
options.text: Read and write access to your calendar
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on permissions and excessive agency.

options.html: Read access to your calendar and inbox
options.text: Read access to your calendar and inbox
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on permissions and excessive agency.

options.html: Write access to your calendar only
options.text: Write access to your calendar only
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on permissions and excessive agency.

options.html: Read access to your calendar only
options.text: Read access to your calendar only
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Reporting on meetings needs viewing the calendar and nothing else.

forms.stemHtml: An agent reads your inbox, including messages from strangers, and can send email. Which features of this setup are legs of the lethal trifecta? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: It can read your private messages
options.text: It can read your private messages
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is access to private data.

options.html: It reads messages written by strangers
options.text: It reads messages written by strangers
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is exposure to untrusted content.

options.html: It can send email to outside addresses
options.text: It can send email to outside addresses
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is a way to communicate externally.

options.html: It runs every morning on a schedule
options.text: It runs every morning on a schedule
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on prompt injection and the lethal trifecta.

forms.stemHtml: Which of these actions by an agent are reversible, so that a mistake costs little? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Writing a draft reply
options.text: Writing a draft reply
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A draft stays with you and can be deleted.

options.html: Making a copy of a file
options.text: Making a copy of a file
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A copy leaves the original untouched.

options.html: Proposing a calendar change
options.text: Proposing a calendar change
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A proposal changes nothing until someone acts on it.

options.html: Publishing a post
options.text: Publishing a post
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on checkpoints and reversibility.

forms.stemHtml: A capable new colleague is handed the request "Summarize this report." Which of the colleague's questions should the prompt have answered? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: How many people wrote the report?
options.text: How many people wrote the report?
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on what a model needs to be told.

options.html: What is the summary going to be used for?
options.text: What is the summary going to be used for?
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is the goal. A summary for a decision differs from one for the record.

options.html: Who is going to read the summary?
options.text: Who is going to read the summary?
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is the audience. What the readers already know changes what to include.

options.html: What form and length should the summary take?
options.text: What form and length should the summary take?
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This covers the output format and a constraint on length.

forms.stemHtml: A teacher wants an AI assistant to explain her school's late-work policy to parents. Which step makes the output about her school's policy?

options.html: Telling the assistant to be accurate and careful
options.text: Telling the assistant to be accurate and careful
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on supplying context.

options.html: Asking the same question in two new conversations
options.text: Asking the same question in two new conversations
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on supplying context.

options.html: Naming the school district in the request
options.text: Naming the school district in the request
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on supplying context.

options.html: Pasting the text of the policy into the prompt
options.text: Pasting the text of the policy into the prompt
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! With the policy supplied, the model can report what it says instead of what such policies usually say.

forms.stemHtml: You give a model three sample announcements and want only their length and layout matched. All three happen to open with a joke. What is the likely result?

options.html: It treats the joke opening as part of the pattern
options.text: It treats the joke opening as part of the pattern
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A feature that appears in every example is treated as part of the pattern, so it helps to say what to match.

options.html: It ignores any feature that all three samples share
options.text: It ignores any feature that all three samples share
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on examples in a prompt.

options.html: It averages the samples and removes all the humor
options.text: It averages the samples and removes all the humor
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on examples in a prompt.

options.html: It stops and asks which features it should follow
options.text: It stops and asks which features it should follow
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on examples in a prompt.

forms.stemHtml: An output runs twice as long as you need and offers a refund you never authorized. Which gap in the prompt does this most likely point to?

options.html: A missing example to imitate
options.text: A missing example to imitate
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on iteration.

options.html: A missing constraint on the result
options.text: A missing constraint on the result
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Length and things that must not be said are limits, and the model can't follow a limit it wasn't given.

options.html: A missing audience for the result
options.text: A missing audience for the result
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on iteration.

options.html: Missing background about the customer
options.text: Missing background about the customer
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on iteration.

forms.stemHtml: A firm gives the same AI writing tool to its newest staff and its most senior staff. Going by the findings of studies of professionals using AI, which result is most likely?

options.html: Senior staff gain most, and the gap between groups widens
options.text: Senior staff gain most, and the gap between groups widens
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on controlled studies of AI at work.

options.html: Neither group changes in speed or in rated quality
options.text: Neither group changes in speed or in rated quality
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on controlled studies of AI at work.

options.html: Newer staff gain most, and the gap between groups narrows
options.text: Newer staff gain most, and the gap between groups narrows
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Studies of writing, support, and consulting work all found the largest gains among weaker or newer workers.

options.html: Both groups gain by exactly the same amount
options.text: Both groups gain by exactly the same amount
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on controlled studies of AI at work.

forms.stemHtml: You have to write a recommendation that you'll be asked to defend. What do you gain by drafting it yourself before involving AI?

options.html: The draft will be finished sooner than an AI draft
options.text: The draft will be finished sooner than an AI draft
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the four roles for AI in writing.

options.html: The structure and conclusion will be your choices
options.text: The structure and conclusion will be your choices
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Drafting first keeps the frame yours. AI can then serve as critic, and you decide which objections hold.

options.html: The AI will be unable to find fault with the draft
options.text: The AI will be unable to find fault with the draft
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the four roles for AI in writing.

options.html: The draft will need no checking of any kind later
options.text: The draft will need no checking of any kind later
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the four roles for AI in writing.

forms.stemHtml: An AI assistant has sorted forty survey comments into themes and quoted supporting comments for each theme. Which is a sound way to verify its work?

options.html: Check nothing, since you supplied the comments yourself
options.text: Check nothing, since you supplied the comments yourself
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on analysis from your own sources.

options.html: Ask the assistant to confirm that its sorting is right
options.text: Ask the assistant to confirm that its sorting is right
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on analysis from your own sources.

options.html: Check a sample, and every point your conclusion uses
options.text: Check a sample, and every point your conclusion uses
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! You don't have to check everything. Check a sample and each point your conclusion rests on, and check more if errors turn up.

options.html: Sort all forty comments again by hand and compare them
options.text: Sort all forty comments again by hand and compare them
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on analysis from your own sources.

forms.stemHtml: A tool that summarizes your documents also asks for permission to edit and delete them. How does that request relate to least privilege?

options.html: It asks for more than the task needs
options.text: It asks for more than the task needs
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Summarizing needs read access. The ability to edit and delete adds risk and adds nothing to the summary.

options.html: It fits the task, since summarizing edits the text
options.text: It fits the task, since summarizing edits the text
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on permissions and excessive agency.

options.html: It lowers risk by keeping files in one place
options.text: It lowers risk by keeping files in one place
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on permissions and excessive agency.

options.html: It matters only if the documents are private
options.text: It matters only if the documents are private
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on permissions and excessive agency.

forms.stemHtml: An agent reads your inbox and can send email. Which changes would remove one leg of the lethal trifecta? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Taking away its ability to send or post anything
options.text: Taking away its ability to send or post anything
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This removes the way to communicate externally.

options.html: Giving it a longer and more detailed instruction
options.text: Giving it a longer and more detailed instruction
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on prompt injection and the lethal trifecta.

options.html: Limiting it to documents that only you have written
options.text: Limiting it to documents that only you have written
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This removes the exposure to untrusted content.

options.html: Telling it to ignore any instructions in the email
options.text: Telling it to ignore any instructions in the email
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on prompt injection and the lethal trifecta.

forms.stemHtml: An agent's task is to remove out-of-date addresses from a mailing list and then email a newsletter to the list. Where do checkpoints belong? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Before it reads the current mailing list
options.text: Before it reads the current mailing list
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on checkpoints and reversibility.

options.html: After it shows its plan, before it starts work
options.text: After it shows its plan, before it starts work
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! An error in the plan carries into every later step, so reviewing the plan catches it early.

options.html: Before it removes addresses from the list
options.text: Before it removes addresses from the list
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Deleting is hard to undo, so it gets an approval step.

options.html: Before it sends the newsletter to the list
options.text: Before it sends the newsletter to the list
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Sending reaches other people and can't be called back.

title: Working Methods
